2.w: “Truly I know that [it is] so. But how can a man be righteous with God?

3.w: If one was delighted to contend with Him, he could not answer Him one [time] out of a thousand.

4.w: [He is] wise of heart and firm of strength; who has hardened [himself] against Him and been whole?

5.w: He moves the mountains, and they do not know when He overturns them in His anger.

6.w: He shakes the earth from its place, and its pillars shudder.

7.w: He speaks to the sun, and it does not rise, and He seals up the stars,

8.w: stretching out the heavens by himself, and treading upon the heights of the sea.

9.w: Making the Bear [and] Orion, and the Pleiades and the chambers of the south,

10.w: doing great [things] until there is no searching out, and wonders until there is no numbering.

11.w: Behold, He passes by over me, and I do not see [Him]; and He moves past, and I do not perceive Him.

12.w: Behold, He snatches away, [and] who will turn Him back? Who shall say to Him, ‘What are You doing?’

13.w: God will not turn aside His nose—beneath Him bowed the helpers of Rahab!

14.w: How then can I answer Him [and] choose my words with Him,

15.w: whom, if I were righteous, I could not answer; to my Judge I would plead for mercy.

16.w: If I called and He answered me, I could not believe that He gives ear [to] my voice—

17.w: [He] who crushes me with a tempest, and multiplies my wounds without cause.

18.w: He does not allow me to return my breath, but He fills me [with] bitterness.

19.w: If [it is] of power, behold, [He is] mighty; and if of justice, who can summon [Him]?

20.w: If I were righteous, my own mouth would declare me wicked; if I were blameless, then it would declare me perverse.

21.w: I [am] blameless; I do not know my soul; I despise my life.

22.w: It [is] one [thing]! [And] upon thus I say, ‘The blameless and the wicked He brings to an end.’

23.w: If the whip kills suddenly, He mocks the despair of the innocent.

24.w: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He covers the faces of its judges—If not, then who is it?

25.w: So my days are swifter than a runner; they flee, not seeing good.

26.w: They pass by with ships of papyrus, like an eagle rushing upon its food.

27.w: If I were to say, ‘I will forget my complaint, let me change my face and smile,’

28.w: I would fear all my sorrows, [and] I know that You will not clear me.

29.w: I am wicked; why then should I labor in vain?

30.w: If I wash myself with water of snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,

31.w: yet into the pit You will plunge me, and my own garments will abhor me.

32.w: For [He is] not a man like I [am], [that] I may answer Him, that we would come together into judgment.

33.w: There is not a mediator between us, to lay his hand upon the two of us,

34.w: tu turn away from me His rod, and not let His terror frighten me.

35.w: I would speak and not be afraid of Him; but I [am] not thus with me.
